scope: Evidence-based research into YouTube's economics, platform use, population, creator earnings, audience demographics, subcultures, competition, content formats and practical monetization strategies.

phases.title: Define the market and research methods
phases.exit: Public source rules, population definitions, eligibility questions and verification methods are documented.

phases.title: Measure YouTube and its creators
phases.exit: Comparable audience, format and subculture measurements are either sourced or explicitly unknown.

phases.title: Understand distribution and earnings
phases.exit: Discovery, policy and earning mechanisms are described with sourced limits and separate revenue units.

phases.title: Study changes and test economic hypotheses
phases.exit: Forecast assumptions and testable monetization pathways are recorded without launching experiments.

deliverables.title: Fees, creator earnings, costs and risks

evidence_rules: Each numeric claim requires source URL, retrieval date, period, geography, population and measurement definition.
An advertised audience estimate is not MAU, and views are not unique people.
Average, median, percentiles and zero earners cannot be conflated.
A community can overlap others, and unknown size remains unknown.
Political audience studies are descriptive; never produce demographic-targeted political persuasion.
No individual sensitive-attribute inference or profiling of children.
Planning is not research; every task remains pending until additional authorization.
Do not create accounts, spend money or publish content as part of research without separate permission.
